note: Locrian over a drone, heard against Phrygian with a Scale selector (only the 5th moves), its home chord 1 ♭3 ♭5 on a new Do (the second key, in place of the old Key choice: the Scale selector is the lesson, so the file has no moves), then a made-up tune that ends every phrase on 1. Missing: a Locrian progression on backing-track (it has a vamp for every other mode), so the tune is made up over the drone, not over a backing track.

exercise.title: Locrian over a drone
exercise.why: Locrian is Phrygian with one more note lowered, the ♭5, so singing the same five notes in both scales over one drone lets you hear the one note that moves.

cells.text:
Press Start exercise below: the drone and the mic start together, and your pitch shows on the staff. Sing the first five notes of the Locrian mode up from the low {{1}} and back down. Sing it on "oo".
The ringed note is {{b5}}, a half step above {{4}}. Once you hear it rub against the drone, sing the same five notes in the Phrygian mode. Use the Scale selector below to change the scale, then press Start exercise to start the drone again.
When you change the scale, only the ringed note moves: it is {{5}} in Phrygian and {{b5}} in Locrian.

Press Start exercise below: the drone and the mic start together, on a new {{1}}. These three notes are the chord on {{1}} in Locrian. Sing {{1}}, {{b3}} and {{b5}} up and back down. Sing it on "oo".
Then leap from the low {{1}} straight up to {{b5}} and back.
Practice until the leap lands without a slide.
In this key the drone is new, and the chord is still {{1}}, {{b3}} and {{b5}}.

Press Start exercise below: the drone and the mic start together, back on the first {{1}}. Make up a short tune from the whole scale, and sing it on "la".
Pass through {{b5}} in every phrase, and end every phrase on {{1}}, so your ear keeps the drone as home.
If a phrase ends on another note and sounds finished there, sing its last two notes again and add {{1}}.
